title: Readable, clean code
idea: Clean code is code a teammate can read once and change safely: honest names, small functions, flat control flow, and no hidden magic values.
points: A name should say what a value holds or what a function returns.
Each function does one thing at one level of detail.
Guard clauses return early, so the main path stays unindented.
Named constants replace magic numbers, so a rule changes in one place.

hero.title: Same result, different cost to change

left.title: Hard to read
items: Nested `if` inside a loop inside a function
Multiplier `0.9` typed inline, maybe in many places

right.title: Clean
items: Named option replaces the mystery flag

hero.verdict: Both print the same numbers. Only one survives the next requirement change.

code.title: Before
code.caption: It works, yet each reader must decode `o`, `t`, `q` and `0.9` before changing anything.

code.title: After
code.caption: Same output. Add an `isStaff` option with its own discount and notice how little you touch.

walk.text: A named constant: the business rule lives in one place.
A tiny helper names one idea: the cost of a line.
An options object makes call sites self-describing instead of `calc(items, 1)`.
Guard clause: reject bad input first, with a clear error type.
Each step reads as a sentence: keep lines with a positive quantity, then add their totals.
The call site now explains itself without a comment.

pitfalls: Do not add comments that repeat the code; rename until the comment is redundant.
Avoid boolean flag parameters; pass a named option or split the function.
Do not shrink code into clever one-liners; optimise for the next reader.

quiz.why: Guard clauses run top to bottom. `0` stops at the second check; `12` passes both guards and is above 9.

takeaway: Write for the next reader: clear names, small functions, early returns.

starters: How long should a function be before I split it?
